screens.title: Overview
screens.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create one finished desktop SaaS product screenshot, approximately 1600x1000, based on the supplied previous page as an exact layout and visual reference. Keep the same white/navy/deep-teal Inter design, sidebar, thin dividers and precise professional spacing. Product and startup are now named "Physical Impact", spelled exactly P H Y S I C A L I M P A C T. Remove every occurrence of AdaptOps. Keep the product wordmark spacious and readable at the top left, workspace "Rivebois Matériaux" beside it. Rivebois is the fictional client company, not the product brand. Top-right "22 Oct 2026", Paul avatar, small "Design proposal". Sidebar: Overview, Watchtower, Actions, Company, Data & Connections. English UI with French proper names.
This is a coherent client account: 6 sites, 200 products, 40 suppliers, 400 customers, 24 programmes, 10,000 order lines. Sites Lille, Centre-Val de Loire, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, Nantes, Lyon, Brussels. Supplier "Arven Isolation"; alternative "Mérial Approvisionnements"; emergency partner "Relais Matériaux". Customer "Bâtirives Construction" with "Programme Cèdre"; protected customer "Ateliers du Parc" with "Programme Aulne". Never show Site A or Site B as a main heading. Secondary native order references may appear in small text: ORD-A, ORD-B. Product label "Isolant référence 100"; SKU ISO100 may be secondary.
Controlled demonstration story: fire reported at the Arven Isolation supplier site. Controlled internal confirmation then attributes a delivery delay to the purchase line. Programme Cèdre needs 8 pallets by 23 Oct. Programme Aulne's 8-pallet reservation for 5 Nov must remain protected. Emergency purchase example €1,420 proposed cost; transfer conditional on replenishment. A separate CRM request is an opportunity to qualify, not demand inferred from the fire. Public historical news is supporting context only. Every screenshot has discreet footer "Fictional client · Synthetic ERP/CRM · Controlled scenario". Screens are visual proposals, not proof of runtime.
Assistant title exactly "Ask Physical Impact", plain speech bubble and A monogram or P monogram, no stars or sparkles. No gradients/glass/glow, robot, generic marketing art, invented ROI, time savings, profit or real-world incident. No em dash. Make the account feel richly populated yet calm, not a toy example. Maintain the supplied reference page's functional content, improving proper names and context.
OVERVIEW. Header "Good morning, Paul." Subtitle "Your company briefing is ready." Under company name show compact meaningful context: "Insulation, timber and panels · France & Belgium", and small inline facts "6 sites", "200 products", "10,000 order lines". Avoid a row of oversized metric cards.
Main briefing headline "Arven Isolation incident: secure the Cèdre delivery". Clear controlled-scenario label. Three sections in one coherent card "What changed": "Fire reported at Arven Isolation. Delivery delay confirmed in the demo record."; "Business impact": "Programme Cèdre needs alternative supply. Programme Aulne remains protected."; "Recommended response": "Review the purchase option and protect existing reservations." Main CTA "Review dossier". Display the €1,420 as proposed purchase cost only. A secondary opportunity row "Bâtirives Construction: additional demand to qualify". Narrow right Watchtower feed shows the fire controlled event at10:32, CRM request at10:28, public historical context at10:14, all origins clear. Bottom contextual Ask Physical Impact input. More credible proper client names and context than the original reference.
